detail.longDescription:
I finally gave up on Chromecast. Jellyfin support has never really been great but it seems that it took a significant dive after the 12.X release. I'm no expert but I think it's because the JF team don't personally use CC and so aren't able to test any changes (totally fair)

YouTube's own CC functionality is getting worse all the time but this is probably vibe-coding related enshittification (they've defo been making changes to the app, but it looks like they're stupid/untested)

Last night I installed LibreElec / Kodi on a Raspberry Pi 4 and it's going great! I was concerned all these years about exposing a "smart tv" interface because I don't want the kids fighting over the physical remote or exploring content we haven't specifically given them access to. Conveniently, we were able to set it up so it only synchronizes the kids-specific libraries. If we want to watch something that's in the regular libraries we are able to "cast" and control everything from the phone.

Playback is much smoother/faster than the CC and it's been able to play videos that the CC just flat out refused to play for unknown reasons.

One problem; During my initial testing, I wasn't able to get audio working... Luckily, a hard reset saved the day

I still have some research to do but I've very happy I made the switch. I want:

- to play around with the account management a bit to figure out how best to support multiple Jellyfin accounts sharing access.
- to see how much I can strip out of the UI. Maybe I still can have the cast-only box flow that we had with the CC.
- to setup tailscale and take it on the road with me to see how well it performs when it's not streaming on the LAN

#selfhosted #homelab #mediaserver  #Jellyfin #LibreElec #Kodi
